items.description:

Turkiye, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan also took part in the exercise, while Kazakhstan attended as an observer country, according to PTV.

items.title: 3 terrorists killed in IBO in KP's Mir Ali: state media
items.description:
Security forces killed three terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in the Mir Ali area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, state broadcaster PTV reported on Wednesday, citing security sources.
The sources added that hideouts of the Fitna al Khawarij were targeted in Mir Ali and surrounding areas. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the terrorists killed during the operation, security sources said.

items.title: Bangladesh women lose ground after quota reform
items.description:
Bangladesh’s 2024 student-led uprising was fuelled by a demand that coveted government jobs be awarded on merit, not through quotas.
The movement succeeded, the government was overthrown, and the quota system was largely scrapped — but the reform has had unintended consequences.
Women are securing a shrinking share of public sector jobs in the Muslim-majority nation of 170 million people.

items.description:

items.title: Somali forces recover oil tanker carrying Pakistani crewmen over 5 months after hijacking by pirates
items.description:

items.title: Public debt surges 76pc to Rs86.7tr in four years
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: With total public debt surging 76 per cent since June 2022 and gross financing needs (GFNs) reaching Rs28.65 trillion for the current fiscal year, the government on Tuesday announced plans to borrow an additional Rs6.86tr to finance the budget deficit.

“Total public debt was recorded at Rs86.7tr at the end of June 2026 from Rs49.3tr at the end of June 2022, a 76pc increase over four years,” the Ministry of Finance said in its Annual Borrowing Plan 2027. It said the total public debt comprised Rs59.4tr in domestic debt and Rs27.3tr equivalent in external debt.

items.title: Saudi Arabia resumes Yanbu oil loading after pipeline restart
items.description:
Saudi Arabia has resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline, according to trade sources and shipping data, improving the outlook for oil exports from the Middle East.
The resumption of Yanbu loadings, halted earlier this month after a drone attack on the pipeline, weighed on global oil prices on Monday as it added to signs of increased flows from the Middle East, from which the US war with Iran has throttled oil shipments.
